doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Lessons with Kenny Davern: listening and martinis
summary: Davern never taught jazz directly but showed upper-register fingerings and listened to records with him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: How did he teach you to play jazz?
Well he never really taught me to play jazz. You really can’t teach anybody to play jazz.
Well that was my next question.

I mean what he did is kind of steer me in the right direction. As a matter of fact I was with him in Sarasota at the Sarasota festival a couple of weeks ago and we were talking about this, because it was thirty years ago you know, practically thirty years ago. And he says, “The way I remember it is that you used to come over to the house and I’d show you a couple of exercises that will help you in your upper register, and then we’d sit down and I’d mix martinis and we’d sit and listen to records for about two or three hours.” And that’s basically what we did. And we would listen to records and he would say, “Now you see what this guy is doing here, see what this is going on here?” And we spent a lot more time hanging out and listening than we actually did playing. But I learned a lot. And he would show me certain fingerings, some of the upper register fingerings that I use, that I’ve become kind of like himself, known for my upper register ability. And most of that stuff is things that he showed me, that he developed himself. So I owe a lot to Kenny.
